title: Copilot Studio: connect agents to MCP servers as tools
summary: Hold: the data-policy navigation omits Edit Policy, and the briefing overstates access to server resources and the absence of administrator prerequisites. Its licensing options also omit restrictions that matter when makers build and publish agents.

claims.quote: Integrate proprietary systems, dynamic knowledge sources, and custom actions into your agentic workflows with MCP support

claims.claim: The roadmap describes reuse of integrations across agents and workflows.
claims.quote: This integration improves reuse across agents and workflows, reduces duplication of integrations

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Makers can extend Copilot Studio agents with MCP server tools.

claims.claim: All tools are on by default when an MCP server is added, with Allow all turned on.

claims.claim: A developer can register an existing MCP server through the Agent 365 CLI in the Agent 365 preview route.

claims.quote: An admin then reviews and approves the request in the Microsoft 365 admin center and grants the required Microsoft Entra permissions.

claims.claim: After approval and consent, server appearance in Copilot Studio environments can take up to 30 minutes.
claims.quote: After approval and consent, the server can take up to 30 minutes to appear in your Copilot Studio environments.

claims.claim: Customers are responsible for tools and resources accessed through non-Microsoft products, including external MCP servers.
claims.quote: When you connect to a non-Microsoft product, including an external MCP server, you're responsible for the tools and resources you access from within Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: The cited Learn pages do not describe charges levied by a third-party MCP server itself.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio MCP third party server pricing license charges. Read the cited MCP and licensing pages. The plugins/cost-considerations search excerpt discusses external-service operating costs, not a third-party MCP vendor's tariff.

claims.claim: The cited Copilot Studio feature documentation applies to agents powered by the standard harness.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness.

claims.claim: No administrator action or administrator-enabled prerequisite is required before makers start using MCP servers.
claims.quote: Publishing doesn't complete setup in a customer's organization. An admin might need to approve or allow the MCP server before people can use it, and users might need to sign in to the service.
claims.fix: Replace the summary's third sentence with 'Review data policies and any server-specific approval requirements before makers add servers.' Replace the broad prerequisite-absence sentence in Why it matters with 'A server can require administrator approval or permission before people can use it.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/mcp-certification. Do not equate absence of a dedicated feature switch with absence of all administrator prerequisites.

claims.claim: The feature is user-opt-in: a maker chooses to add an MCP server, with no dedicated MCP feature-enablement switch documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio MCP admin enable disable tenant switch rollout generative orchestration. Read agent-extend-action-mcp, mcp-add-existing-server-to-agent, mcp-add-components-to-agent and admin-data-loss-prevention. Makers add servers; no dedicated MCP client feature switch was documented.

claims.claim: Learn documents no staged rollout for the general Copilot Studio MCP connection capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio MCP rollout tenant enable switch no action required. Read the cited MCP connection pages and the returned Copilot Studio UX release-note excerpt. No staged rollout for this general capability was stated; the separate registry tool-control rollout is acknowledged.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether this feature changes existing tenant behavior when nobody acts.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio MCP rollout tenant enable switch no action required. Read the roadmap record and cited MCP connection pages; they describe maker setup, not an automatic migration or a tenant do-nothing outcome.

claims.claim: An existing data policy can be opened for connector blocking through Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Add an environment > Assign connectors > connector > Block.
claims.quote: To edit an existing data policy, select the data policy and select Edit Policy.
claims.fix: Insert the required Edit Policy action after policy in both front matter and the rendered table. Use 'Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Add an environment > Assign connectors > connector > Block'. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy GUID> -Classification Blocked -Connectors $connectors moves connectors into the policy's Blocked group.
claims.quote: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy [-PolicyName] <String> [-Classification] <String> [-Connectors] <Object[]> ... Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Block restricts that server and all its tools across the organization.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools, and then select the Registry tab. ... Select an MCP server ... Select Block to restrict the server across your organization ... Blocking an MCP server disables all the tools it exposes.
